issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising second-appellate jurisdiction may interfere with factual findings only within the limits of that jurisdiction, and must formulate a proper substantial question of law before deciding the second appeal.
material_facts: The dispute arose from a suit for specific performance, dismissed by the trial court and on first appeal.
The High Court reversed the first appellate court’s findings concerning readiness and willingness and the interpretation of the sale agreement.
The High Court framed questions of law, but the Supreme Court held that the questions did not meet the requirements for substantial questions of law under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
The claimant had paid a substantial part of the consideration and substantial sums towards conversion charges and measurement fees.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s judgment was set aside and the matter remitted to it for fresh consideration after formulating a proper substantial question of law. The Supreme Court did not decide whether specific performance should ultimately be granted.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the High Court’s jurisdiction in a second appeal is limited, and a substantial question of law must be formulated. Whether a plaintiff was ready and willing to perform is not by itself necessarily a substantial question of law. A substantial question may arise where relevant facts or vital documents are ignored, irrelevant considerations influence the decision, evidence is misread, or findings are perverse or unsupported by evidence; a different view on the same facts alone is insufficient. The Court relied on Vidhyadhar v. Manikrao, Iswar Bhai C. Patel v. Harihar Behera, Commissioner of Customs (Preventive) v. Vijay Dasharath Patel, Madan Lal v. Gopi, Collector of Customs v. Swastic Woollens (P) Ltd., Metroark Ltd. v. CCE, W.B. Electricity Regulatory Commission v. CESC Ltd., Commissioner of Customs v. Bureau Veritas, Dutta Cycle Stores v. Gita Devi Sultania, and P. Chandrasekharan v. S. Kanakarajan.

predicates.second_appeal_from_appellate_findings: The proceeding is a second appeal challenging findings made by the courts below in a civil case.
predicates.proper_substantial_question_missing: The High Court decided the second appeal without formulating a question that properly qualifies as a substantial question of law.
predicates.claimant_paid_substantial_consideration_: The claimant had paid a substantial part of the agreed consideration and substantial costs connected with conversion of the land.
predicates.high_court_judgment_set_aside_and_matter: The High Court’s judgment is set aside and the matter is returned to it for fresh consideration after proper formulation of a substantial question of law.

issues.definition: When a second appeal lacks a properly formulated substantial question of law, and the claimant has made substantial payments, the High Court’s judgment is set aside and the matter is returned for fresh consideration.
